text: βαίνει ὁ Δεινόσαυρος πρὸς τὸν Ἔμπορον. ὁ Ἔμπορος πωλεῖ ἄρτον καὶ μῆλα καὶ ὕδωρ.
objects: a small woven flax sack, tan with a drawstring, soft and slightly wrinkled, sized to fit in Dinosaur’s hands.
a merchant’s stall table of chalk-white wood with neat woven baskets and a blue-painted edge.
a round rustic loaf of bread with a golden-brown crust and a cross-slashed top, about the size of Dinosaur’s head.
a basket of red apples, glossy and firm, heaped in a shallow wicker tray.
a tall clay water jar, terracotta with a simple blue band near the shoulder.
artist_notes: Soft daylight inside the stoa; keep columns and tidy displays in view.
positioning: Dinosaur approaches from left, front three-quarter view, looking at the merchant behind the stall, stopping before the table.
Emporos stands behind the stall, front view leaning slightly forward with a welcoming smile, looking at Dinosaur.
The small woven sack hangs at Dinosaur’s right side, closed with its drawstring.
The merchant’s stall table spans mid-right at waist height, baskets neatly arranged on top.
The round rustic loaf sits in the front basket atop a cloth, clearly visible.
The basket of red apples rests to one side of the bread, mounded high.
The tall clay water jar stands near the back corner of the table.
